instruction: Read docs/TASK_PHASE15.md FIRST, section 2.3 (Names, the tests.helpers.legacy_db entry). You own exactly one file: tests/helpers.py, the shared test helpers module. Keep everything already in it byte for byte (every class and function, their docstrings and behaviour) and ADD one function legacy_db(phase) -> str. phase is 13 or 14. It creates a brand-new tempfile.mkdtemp() directory and in it one sqlite file made with plain sqlite3 (never with ethsc.store.Store, never PRAGMA journal_mode -- the file stays in the default rollback journal mode 'delete'): tables codes (code_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, size INTEGER, skeleton_hash TEXT, selectors TEXT, proxy_kind TEXT, proxy_target TEXT, code BLOB, std_proxy INTEGER), addresses (address TEXT PRIMARY KEY, code_id TEXT, block INTEGER, origin TEXT) plus a last column implementation TEXT when phase is 14, the index addresses_code_id on addresses(code_id), progress (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, block INTEGER) with no updated_at column, seeds (address TEXT PRIMARY KEY, code_id TEXT, label TEXT), ledger (day TEXT, method TEXT, credits INTEGER); no events table. Fill it from block_codes(): every address lowercased at block 26077729 with origin NULL (and implementation NULL); an address whose code is '0x' gets code_id NULL; every other code once in codes, its columns from ethsc.fingerprint.fingerprint(code): code_id, size, skeleton_hash, selectors as json.dumps of the list, proxy_kind/proxy_target from fingerprint's proxy (NULL when None), the code bytes, std_proxy 1 or 0. Then the row ('progress', 26077729). Commit, close the connection, return the path. Expected over the fixture: 130 codes (17 with std_proxy 1), 206 addresses, 147 with code. Give it a docstring like the other helpers. No test file of your own: the acceptance probes legacy_db(13) and legacy_db(14) and runs the full suite.

Read docs/TASK_PHASE15.md FIRST (sections 1-4, 6 and 7), then in contour.yaml group store: Store Codes And Contracts (the paragraph 'Phase 15 (the dashboard)', examples 16-17), Track Progress (whole, example 2), Base Counts (origin_counts, example 4), Record Events (new, whole), Open Read Only (new, whole), dataObjects Code Database and Event. You own ethsc/store.py and tests/test_store_p15.py. In ethsc/store.py: (1) the schema script gains CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT, block INTEGER, at TEXT, address TEXT, seed_address TEXT, label TEXT, score REAL, origin TEXT, old_impl TEXT, new_impl TEXT) -- no AUTOINCREMENT -- and progress gains updated_at TEXT; (2) Store.__init__(self, path, readonly=False): a writable open runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL as the first statement after connect, then the schema script and the existing migrations, plus ALTER TABLE progress ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT when the column is missing (same PRAGMA table_info pattern, no UPDATE of old rows); a readonly open connects to 'file:' + path + '?mode=ro' with uri=True and runs nothing else that writes (no pragma, no schema script, no ALTER, no std_proxy fill); (3) class ReadOnlyStoreError(Exception), raised at the top of every write method (put_code, put_address, set_implementation, set_progress, add_seed, remove_seed, spend, add_events) of a readonly store before any SQL; (4) set_progress also writes updated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc) formatted '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'; progress_at() reads it; (5) add_events(events), events(after_id=0, limit=100), event_counts() exactly as Record Events says: one transaction, ValueError for a kind other than ALERT/UPGRADE with nothing written, newest first, lowercase addresses, eleven keys, score a float; (6) origin_counts(since_block=None) with one SELECT ... GROUP BY; (7) a readonly store tolerates exactly the three missing additions of an older file (no events table, no progress.updated_at, no addresses.implementation) as Open Read Only says -- detect them once at open with PRAGMA table_info / sqlite_master, then answer [] / zeros / None. Keep every existing method, signature and docstring behaviour; Store(path) with one positional argument still works. Keep the module docstring and extend it by one sentence for phase 15. tests/helpers.py is rewritten by another card in your generation, so it is not in your slice: your smoke tests may import from it only temp_store() (a fresh Store in a new tempfile.mkdtemp() directory, no arguments) and load_hex(name) (bytes of tests/fixtures/<name>), or build a Store on os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'e.sqlite') themselves. Your own test file tests/test_store_p15.py is SMOKE ONLY: 1 to 5 test_* functions (an import, one happy path per new function, one tolerant case); compare scalars and short values (lengths, counters, single elements), never whole fixture-sized lists or dicts; no maxDiff. Completeness is judged by a probe in the acceptance and by a separate judge card. Import every stub and fixture loader from tests/helpers.py (temp_store, block_store, block_codes, load_hex, FakeRpc, InterruptAfter); do not define your own Fake* classes. Every file a test writes goes into a tempfile.mkdtemp() directory -- nothing in the project tree. Python 3.9 syntax, standard library only.

You own the NEW module ethsc/dashboard.py and tests/test_dashboard_p15.py. Write respond(db_path, target, static_dir=None, now=None, cache=None) -> (status, content_type, body_bytes) and make_server(db_path, host='127.0.0.1', port=8080, static_dir=None) -> http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer exactly as the Contour says. Import only from the standard library and ethsc (ethsc.store.Store, ethsc.cluster.build_clusters); the only network-family import allowed is http.server -- query strings are split by hand on '&' and '=', and percent-decoding of the path is a small hand-written function. Read the store only through its public methods (readonly Store per request, closed in a finally). Every answer is computed by respond; the request handler class (a BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass) only calls respond for GET, sends 405 JSON for every other method (do_POST, do_PUT, do_DELETE, do_HEAD, do_PATCH), writes Content-Type and Content-Length, and overrides log_message to write nothing. The clusters cache reads time.monotonic() through 'import time'. Any exception inside respond becomes 500 {'error': one line}; never a traceback in a body. Static files: resolve with os.path.realpath and refuse any path outside the static directory. Your smoke tests call respond directly; at most one test may start make_server on ('127.0.0.1', 0) and talk to it with a raw socket.socket (never urllib or http.client: the acceptance blocks getaddrinfo). You own ethsc/ingest.py and tests/test_ingest_p15.py. Change follow_chain only (ingest_block and every other function stay as they are): for each block, build two recording sinks that append what they receive to block-local lists and then forward the same list to on_alerts / on_upgrades when those are not None; hand them to ingest_block instead of on_alerts / on_upgrades. Wrap the ingest_block call so that, in a finally (after the existing ledger charges of charge_after), when the block delivered at least one alert or upgrade, follow_chain calls store.add_events once with the block's alerts first (each dict(alert, kind='ALERT', block=block, at=at)) and then its upgrades (each {'kind': 'UPGRADE', 'block': block, 'at': at, 'address': u['address'], 'old_impl': u['old'], 'new_impl': u['new']}), with one at per block = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'). The finally runs on the normal return, on an incomplete block and on KeyboardInterrupt (which then propagates); the events of a complete block are written before its set_progress. Everything else -- summary keys and values, stats, ledger, the order and content of what on_alerts/on_upgrades receive -- is unchanged. Extend the follow_chain docstring by a short 'Phase 15 (events)' paragraph. Your edit is about 30 lines; return the whole file with every other line unchanged.
